# FLUX 3 layout with boxes

**Workflow:** [`flux3/flux3-layout-boxes.json`](../flux3/flux3-layout-boxes.json)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Family | `flux3` |
| Nodes | 8 |
| Links | 6 |
| Paid API calls per run | **1** |

---

Place every element yourself: a caption that names each element as `<id>`, plus one box per element, joined into the single prompt string FLUX 3 reads layouts from.

Boxes are **[top, left, bottom, right]** on a **0–1000** grid from the top-left corner. `[0, 0, 500, 500]` is the top-left quarter whatever the frame, because the grid stretches with it — so `aspect_ratio` here is **1:1**, the shape the boxes were drawn for.

Each **Box Element** adds one row and passes the table on; chain as many as you need. **Layout Prompt** joins the caption and the table, and prints a warning if a row's id never appears in the caption. Its `rows_json` takes a pasted JSON array too, such as one copied from the BFL docs.

Boxes guide placement, they do not clip. Give text its own box and quote the words in `desc`. A box of roughly 40 × 25 pixels is often too small for a new element to appear.

The Box and Layout nodes are free; only the FLUX 3 node is billed.

`variation` is not sent to the API — flux-3-image has no seed. It is **fixed** here so a rerun with nothing changed costs nothing; bump it (or set it to *randomize*) for a fresh take. `expanded_prompt` is `result.prompt`, the prompt the model actually used after expanding yours.

## The prompt lives in one node

The **Shared Prompt** node feeds the prompt in this graph, so there is one
place to edit it. It emits a plain string, **not** a list. That is the difference between it and **Prompt
List**, which would make each node it feeds run once per line and multiply what the graph
costs.
